title: Duplicate: Ellington's band at the Kentucky Club

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I didn't have the chance to feel any remorse or anything, because I went right out of the pan into the fire, so to speak. I went with him like that, the next night in the Kentucky Club. He only had one trumpet, Bubber Milley, Bubba Marley. And he had about eight pieces there, with me.

And, well, they were recording again, recording records. And you jump right into records with Duke. And we played there, and played there quite a while. You heard of Green Sonny Grier, he was on drums.
And Otto Hardwick and Freddy Guy. Of course, he died, he was a guitar player. And Tricky Sam was on trombone. Yeah, he died, too. And Bro, Bro was on bass. Brand
Yeah. Well, I guess Sonny is the only one left.
Yeah, yeah. Bro was on bass. Bro -- after he left Duke, he opened up a pool parlor and I saw him one day. I used to pass by, he'd always come out and call me, and we'd stop and talk about old times.
So then he told me one day he was giving it up, he was going back to New Orleans, his home. And I shook hands with him and wished him well. Never saw him again.
